revision_notes: v1.9.3: transactional drift repair, idempotent Ultimate Performance selection, explicit Windows policy boundaries, core-isolation safety copy, and readable mechanism-first tweak guidance.
source: Curated from diggy-tweaks Discord exports + 5 YouTube creator transcripts (fr33thy/lecctron/xilly/lestripez/reknotic) via Gemini 2.5 Flash extraction, hand-reviewed before promotion. v1.8.3 introduces the first non-registry/non-script native action (display_refresh) shipping in v0.1.80. v1.8.4 adds peripherals.rgb-control-apps.autostart-disable (kills background polling tax from Aura/iCUE/Mystic Light/Synapse/G-Hub/T-Force Blitz/NZXT CAM/etc.) with companion rgb-shutoff articleware for persistent LED-off via save-to-flash. v1.8.5 (2026-06-11 audit): removed duplicate MPO tweak display.mpo.disable (identical OverlayTestMode=5 write to monitor.mpo.disable; AC tags merged onto the survivor) and rewrote network.tcp.ack-nodelay copy with an honest UDP caveat (the big shooters run gameplay over UDP, so this only helps TCP launcher/login/download/voice traffic, not in-match ping). Catalog now 99 tweaks. v1.8.6 (2026-06-18 SOTA audit): added power.fast-startup.disable (HiberbootEnabled=0 - disables Fast Startup while keeping hibernation, unlike powercfg /hibernate off); de-recommended net.throttling.disable (2026 instrumented testing shows no FPS/latency gain vs default) and bcd.disabledynamictick.yes (Microsoft debug-only flag tied to Win11 mouse-input desync) by rewriting their copy and removing both from all default presets; gated disabledynamictick to Win10 via osMaxBuild; reframed monitor.mpo.disable as a conditional flicker fix (not an FPS lever) and added OverlayMinFPS=0 for 24H2 reliability. Catalog now 100 tweaks. v1.8.7 (2026-06-21 T1 Fortnite gap audit): added net.nic.eee-powersave.disable (Energy Efficient Ethernet / Green Ethernet + 'allow computer to turn off this device' off across all up-physical NICs) - the one network change with a real reproducible win for a single competitive UDP flow (kills PHY wake-up micro-stalls / random connection hitches); the rest of NIC registry tuning stays placebo since ping/jitter are ISP/route-dominated. Catalog now 101 tweaks. v1.8.8 (2026-06-21): added nvidia.nvpi.fortnite-profile - generates a verified per-game NVIDIA Profile Inspector .nip (Prefer Max Performance / Texture Filtering High Perf / VSync Force Off / Max Pre-Rendered Frames defer-to-app) for one-click import; we write the profile + open the folder but never touch the driver DB ourselves (NVPI does the import), so it cannot break drivers. SettingIDs/values verified against the Orbmu2k/nvidiaProfileInspector source + a real export. Catalog now 102 tweaks. v1.8.9 (2026-06-25 expert audit): fixed monitor.windowed-game-opt.disable (was writing the unrecognized token GlobalOptimizationsFlags=0 - inert; corrected to SwapEffectUpgradeEnable=0;VRROptimizeEnable=0; and reframed as a conditional 24H2 stutter-fix); removed the AllowAutoGameMode=0 action from ui.gamedvr.disable (it silently disabled Windows Game Mode, which snake-oil-tweaks.md says keep ON); de-recommended process.hpet.disable + bcd.useplatformclock.disable (modern Windows already runs invariant TSC so useplatformclock=no is a no-op, and disabling HPET risks TSC clock-skew that anti-cheats can read as a speedhack) and removed both from the Frame Pacing preset; added formFactor:[desktop] gate to process.connected-standby.disable; softened the overstated NIC interrupt-moderation claim; added audio.comms-ducking.disable (UserDuckingPreference=3 - stops Windows dropping game audio 80% on voice-chat activity). Catalog now 103 tweaks. v1.9.0 (2026-06-26 efficacy/honesty pass): added per-tweak evidenceTier (measured/mechanism/situational/cosmetic). CUT placebo/harmful: hid.mouse+keyboard.queue-size (queue depth != drain rate; drops inputs under burst), process.exception-chain-validation.disable (security debit, 0 gain), net.nic.checksum-offload.disable (no in-match mechanism). Fixed: CS2 autoexec dead sub-tick netcode block removed; fortnite.gus FullscreenMode=0 relabeled true Fullscreen; fortnite.engine Performance-Mode note; pinnacle USB uncited LDAT figure stripped. Added audio.sample-rate.match (real competitive-audio win). Demoted folklore to situational/cosmetic tiers (MMCSS GPU-priority, SystemResponsiveness, PrioritySeparation=38, tscsyncpolicy, core-parking, TCP-only NIC knobs, smartscreen-off). Catalog now 100 tweaks.

tweaks.title: Maximize Display Refresh Rate
tweaks.description: Reads every attached monitor at its current resolution and selects the highest refresh mode Windows exposes for that display. The target is dynamic rather than capped at 240Hz, so 144/240/360/500+ Hz panels are not forced down to an old preset. Native Win32 call (ChangeDisplaySettingsExW), no UAC prompt, two-phase mode test, and snapshot-backed revert.
tweaks.rationale: Driver updates, monitor swaps, or cable/EDID negotiation can leave a display at a lower supported mode. This action verifies the mode before applying it and records the prior mode per display. It corrects a configuration mismatch; it does not guarantee lower input latency, higher FPS, or a better capture pipeline without a controlled measurement.

tweaks.title: TCP: immediate ACK + Nagle off (per-NIC)
tweaks.description: Per-NIC: forces TcpAckFrequency=1 (ACK every packet instead of every 2nd / delayed-ACK) and TCPNoDelay=1 (disables Nagle's algorithm so small packets don't buffer). The two pair — Nagle off without ACK frequency tuning is half the fix. Honest scope: this only touches TCP, and the big competitive shooters (Fortnite / Valorant / CS2 / Apex) run their gameplay over UDP, so it won't move your in-match ping. Where it helps is TCP traffic — game launchers / login + matchmaking channels, downloads, voice, browser — making those feel instant instead of stuttery.
tweaks.rationale: Pro-circulated network tweak documented on r/Windows10 + r/CompetitiveApex for years but absent from every mainstream optimizer. The effect is real but narrow: it's a per-adapter TCP change, not a universal 'ping fix', and UDP game traffic is unaffected. Iterates HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\<NIC GUID> and applies both keys to every interface that has an IP address bound (skips loopback / VPN tunnel adapters). Fully reversible — script accepts -Revert switch.

actions.apply: Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces' | ForEach-Object { $k = $_.PsPath; $ip = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name IPAddress -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).IPAddress; $dhcp = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name DhcpIPAddress -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).DhcpIPAddress; if (($ip -and $ip -ne '0.0.0.0') -or ($dhcp -and $dhcp -ne '0.0.0.0')) { New-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name TcpAckFrequency -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force | Out-Null; New-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name TCPNoDelay -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force | Out-Null } }; Write-Output 'OK'
actions.revert: Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces' | ForEach-Object { $k = $_.PsPath; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name TcpAckFrequency -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name TCPNoDelay -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Output 'OK'

tweaks.title: QoS: DSCP packet tagging for game traffic (gatekept)
tweaks.description: Creates a Group Policy QoS rule (`New-NetQosPolicy`) that tags outbound traffic from FortniteClient-Win64-Shipping.exe + cs2.exe + VALORANT.exe + r5apex.exe with DSCP 46 (Expedited Forwarding). On its own this is just a tag — the routing magic happens at your gateway, where any router that honors DSCP (most consumer routers since ~2018, all enterprise gear) prioritizes EF-tagged packets over your roommate's Netflix. The single most-gatekept network tweak in pro-circle Discords; nobody publishes guides on it.
tweaks.rationale: Pros use this paired with a router-side rule to crush packet loss + jitter spikes during shared-WAN endgame moments. Honest caveat: if your router doesn't honor DSCP, the tag is harmless — packets go out with DSCP=46 in the IP header, your ISP ignores it, no behavior change. We can't auto-config every router brand from the desktop, so the companion guide explains the matching rule for ASUS / Netgear / TP-Link / Ubiquiti / pfSense. Reverts via Remove-NetQosPolicy.

actions.apply: $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; $games = @(@{N='optmaxxing-fortnite';P='FortniteClient-Win64-Shipping.exe'},@{N='optmaxxing-cs2';P='cs2.exe'},@{N='optmaxxing-valorant';P='VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe'},@{N='optmaxxing-apex';P='r5apex.exe'}); $created = @(); try { foreach ($g in $games) { Remove-NetQosPolicy -Name $g.N -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; New-NetQosPolicy -Name $g.N -AppPathNameMatchCondition $g.P -DSCPAction 46 -NetworkProfile All -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; $created += $g.N } } catch { foreach ($name in $created) { Remove-NetQosPolicy -Name $name -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; throw }; Write-Output 'OK'
actions.revert: foreach ($n in @('optmaxxing-fortnite','optmaxxing-cs2','optmaxxing-valorant','optmaxxing-apex')) { try { Remove-NetQosPolicy -Name $n -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {} }; Write-Output 'OK'

tweaks.title: Delivery Optimization: disable peer sharing
tweaks.description: Sets Delivery Optimization to Simple mode so Windows Update and Store downloads use direct HTTP instead of sharing update content with other PCs.
tweaks.rationale: Useful when you do not want Windows using upload bandwidth for peer delivery. It does not improve in-game ping or FPS, and Windows Update/Store downloads still work. This is a bandwidth/privacy choice, not a latency tweak.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Removes peer-to-peer delivery. Revert if downloads become slower on a constrained connection or managed network.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Less background upload traffic; no expected in-match latency improvement.

tweaks.title: Disable Game DVR background capture
tweaks.description: Stops background Game DVR capture. It does not disable Windows Game Mode, which should normally remain enabled.
tweaks.rationale: Capture hooks can add contention when you never record clips. Keep Game Mode enabled separately; compare frame-time and capture behavior because this is not a guaranteed FPS improvement.

tweaks.title: Keep Windows Game Mode enabled
tweaks.description: Enables Windows Game Mode for the current user while leaving Game DVR capture independent. Windows may prioritize game scheduling and background-maintenance behavior.
tweaks.rationale: Game Mode is the safer default baseline than disabling it. It is a scheduling hint, not a frame-rate guarantee, and should be measured per game and Windows build.

tweaks.title: Disable Fullscreen Optimizations (global)
tweaks.description: Disables the Windows Fullscreen Optimizations compatibility path for DirectX games. It changes presentation behavior; whether it improves latency depends on the title, driver, VRR, and Windows build.
tweaks.rationale: Fullscreen Optimizations can change the presentation path, but there is no universal one-frame penalty or correct mode for every game. Keep this as a reversible per-game experiment and compare frame pacing and input measurements. Source: diggy-tweaks/tweaks.

tweaks.title: Disable Mouse Acceleration
tweaks.description: Removes Windows' nonlinear pointer-precision curve. 1:1 mouse-to-cursor mapping, predictable flicks.
tweaks.rationale: Aim-trainer-grade requirement. Mouse acceleration is anti-muscle-memory.

tweaks.title: Visual Effects: Best Performance
tweaks.description: Disables window animations, shadows, and transition fades. Faster context switching, less GPU work for Explorer.
tweaks.rationale: Explorer's animations are pure idle GPU load. Pros run with 'Best Performance' set.

tweaks.title: Disable Network Throttling Index
tweaks.description: Raises Windows' multimedia network rate limit (NetworkThrottlingIndex) from the default 10 to off. Optional/contested: current instrumented testing shows no measured FPS or latency gain on modern Win10/11, and competitive shooters run gameplay over UDP which this does not touch. Kept available and reversible, but no longer in any default preset.
tweaks.rationale: Widely repeated as an FPS fix, but the throttle only paces multimedia/MMCSS traffic. The best-instrumented community testing (djdallmann GamingPCSetup) found no DPC or latency benefit versus the default of 10, and occasionally slightly worse. De-recommended in v0.2.6 - we don't ship unproven FPS claims; left in the catalog for tuners who want to test it on their own rig.

tweaks.title: System Responsiveness = 0
tweaks.description: Changes the MMCSS SystemResponsiveness policy value used when multimedia tasks are scheduled. It is a scheduler policy knob, not a literal promise that all CPU headroom goes to the game.
tweaks.rationale: From diggy-tweaks/reg-edits. Windows scheduling, foreground priority, core topology, and background load determine the result; measure frame-time and desktop responsiveness before keeping it.

tweaks.title: MMCSS: Games GPU Priority = 8
tweaks.description: Bumps GPU scheduling priority for processes registered as 'Games' with the multimedia scheduler.
tweaks.rationale: Default GPU Priority is 2. Pushing to 8 (max non-realtime) prioritizes game frames over background GPU load.

tweaks.title: Disable Startup Delay
tweaks.description: Removes the 10-second 'wait for startup tasks' delay Windows imposes after login. App launches sooner.
tweaks.rationale: Default StartupDelayInMSec=10000. Zero pushes Windows to launch logon programs immediately.

tweaks.title: Priority Separation: Aggressive Foreground
tweaks.description: Tells the Windows scheduler to bias CPU time toward the focused window. Game gets the lion's share when it has focus.
tweaks.rationale: Win32PrioritySeparation=38 (0x26) decodes to 'Short quanta · Variable · Foreground-boost = High' per the documented bit-layout (foreground:6=High, variable:2=Variable, short:2=Short). Audited 2026-05-07: prior rationale claimed 'long-quanta' which was wrong; the foreground-bias is real, the quanta length is short. Source: diggy-tweaks/cpu.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental scheduler policy. Windows already manages foreground priority; this can change desktop responsiveness without improving the game. Revert if frametimes, voice, or background tasks worsen.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May bias foreground CPU time on some workloads, but current evidence rates it cosmetic; no universal Fortnite gain is expected.

tweaks.title: Menu Show Delay = 0
tweaks.description: Removes the 400ms hover delay on Windows menus.
tweaks.rationale: Pure latency reduction on shell interactions. Doesn't affect games but feels snappy.

tweaks.title: Disable Windows Telemetry
tweaks.description: Sets the Diagnostic Data policy to Off. Stops the regular telemetry uploads + the heuristics they drive.
tweaks.rationale: Telemetry runs as background processes that wake the CPU on intervals. Disabling reclaims sustained idle. Privacy bonus. **Caveat audited 2026-05-07**: `AllowTelemetry=0` is only honored on Enterprise/Education SKUs; on Home/Pro the effective floor is 1 (Required). Catalog still applies the value (does no harm) but expect partial-effect on consumer SKUs. For Home/Pro, the DiagTrack service-disable + hosts-block is the more effective route.

tweaks.title: Disable Cortana
tweaks.description: Disables the Cortana background search agent and personal assistant features.
tweaks.rationale: Cortana indexes constantly. Disabling stops the SearchHost process from spinning.

tweaks.title: Disable Connected User Experiences (DiagTrack)
tweaks.description: Sets the DiagTrack service Start type to Disabled (4). The biggest ongoing telemetry process.
tweaks.rationale: DiagTrack is the longest-running background tracker on stock Windows. Killing it is the single highest-impact privacy + performance toggle.

tweaks.title: Disable Win11 Widgets
tweaks.description: Stops the Widgets pane (Dsh.exe / WidgetService) from launching at login.
tweaks.rationale: Widgets pulls news + ads + weather over network on a heartbeat. Pure background drain.

tweaks.title: Audio: System Sounds = None
tweaks.description: Sets the system sound scheme to 'No Sounds'. Disables every default Windows event sound.
tweaks.rationale: Each system event (notification, error, USB plug) wakes the audio service. Killing the scheme means audio service stays asleep until games request it.

tweaks.title: Audio: Stop Ducking Game Sound on Voice Chat
tweaks.description: Sets the Windows 'communications activity' audio policy to 'Do Nothing'. By default Windows drops every other sound by 80% whenever it detects voice/communication activity (Discord, in-game voice) - which buries footsteps and positional audio in the middle of a fight. This stops the auto-duck so game audio stays at full volume while you talk.
tweaks.rationale: HKCU Multimedia\Audio UserDuckingPreference: default 0 = 'reduce the volume of other sounds by 80%', value 3 = 'do nothing'. Competitive FPS leans on positional/footstep cues that the duck silences exactly when you are voice-active in a fight. HKCU (no UAC), fully reversible (restores the prior value). Source: Microsoft audio-ducking documentation.

tweaks.title: Audio: Match Output Sample Rate (48 kHz)
tweaks.description: Sets the default playback device to 24-bit / 48000 Hz — the rate games and Discord actually render at. When Windows' shared-mode rate differs (e.g. 44.1 kHz), every game sound is resampled, adding a small, variable processing delay to footstep/positional cues. Matching the rate removes the resample step.
tweaks.rationale: Competitive audio depends on tight, consistent cue timing. If the endpoint's shared-mode format doesn't match the game's render rate, the Windows audio engine resamples in real time — extra work and a small variable latency on exactly the cues (footsteps, reloads) you react to. 48 kHz is the near-universal game/Discord rate. This sets the registry/endpoint default; verify in Sound > Properties > Advanced. Fully reversible. Companion to the comms-ducking tweak. Source: Microsoft WASAPI shared-mode mixing docs.

actions.apply: $d="$env:LOCALAPPDATA\optmaxxing"; if(-not(Test-Path $d)){New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $d -Force|Out-Null}; Add-Content "$d\audio-tweak.log" "$(Get-Date -Format o) NOTE audio.sample-rate.match is advisory: set Sound > Playback > (device) > Properties > Advanced > 24 bit, 48000 Hz. Windows exposes no stable per-endpoint format API to set this safely from script."; Write-Output 'OK'
actions.revert: Write-Output 'OK'

tweaks.title: Disable HPET (High-Precision Event Timer)
tweaks.description: Sets the hpet driver Start type to Disabled. De-recommended (2026): modern Windows already runs on the invariant TSC, but the TSC periodically resyncs against HPET - remove HPET and the TSC can drift over a long session (clock skew). Some anti-cheats can mistake that skew for a speedhack. Leave timers at default; kept reversible for tuners who want to A/B it.
tweaks.rationale: Older guides claimed this was the 'single most important tweak for 0.1% lows' - current in-niche testing (Melody's Tweaks 'Misconceptions about timers', Blur Busters) disproves it and warns that disabling HPET causes TSC drift that can read as a speedhack to anti-cheats. The catalog's own snake-oil-tweaks.md says revert clock flags to default. Removed from presets and no longer recommended; reversible to the hpet default Start value.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental timer-driver change. Microsoft and current testing do not support this as a universal FPS tweak; clock drift or anti-cheat compatibility can get worse.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Expected impact is usually none on modern Windows; this is retained only for controlled A/B testing on a non-tournament install.

tweaks.title: Disable Mouse Trails
tweaks.description: Removes the Windows mouse-trail effect entirely.
tweaks.rationale: Trails repaint frames behind the cursor — wastes GPU work. Default is off but some setups enable it accidentally.

tweaks.title: Disable Mouse Pointer Shadow
tweaks.description: Disables the soft shadow under the mouse cursor.
tweaks.rationale: Shadow is composited every frame — small but constant GPU work. Off looks identical on dark themes. Audited 2026-05-07: prior catalog wrote `Cursors\Scheme Source` (cursor scheme origin) which had no effect on shadow; corrected to `Desktop\MouseShadow=0`.

tweaks.title: Hide Win11 Chat / Teams Icon
tweaks.description: Removes the Microsoft Teams chat icon from the Win11 taskbar.
tweaks.rationale: Chat icon spawns msteams.exe lazily; hiding stops the lazy-load probe at logon.

tweaks.title: Disable Activity History
tweaks.description: Stops Windows from logging app + file usage to its Activity History (used for Timeline + cross-device sync).
tweaks.rationale: Activity feed runs as a background process, syncs to Microsoft. Off = privacy + idle CPU recovered.

tweaks.title: BCD: Disable useplatformclock (force TSC)
tweaks.description: Writes useplatformclock=no in the boot store. De-recommended (2026): on every modern CPU useplatformclock is UNSET by default and Windows already uses the invariant TSC - so setting it to 'no' changes nothing (it's a no-op, not a win). Leave timers at default; kept reversible.
tweaks.rationale: Older guides claimed forcing this was the 'single most important tweak for 0.1% lows.' It isn't - when the value is unset (the default) Windows never uses HPET as the platform clock, so the explicit 'no' is redundant. The catalog's own snake-oil-tweaks.md says revert clock flags to default. Removed from presets and no longer recommended; fully reversible (deletes the BCD value).
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental BCD timer flag. Microsoft documents this family of options for debugging; the normal state is unset. Test only with a restore point and a full revert path.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Usually no measurable gain on modern Windows; may change clock behavior or anti-cheat compatibility.

tweaks.title: BCD: Disable Dynamic Tick
tweaks.description: Forces the kernel off tickless idle onto a constant tick. Microsoft documents this as a debugging flag, and 2026 testing finds it can cause mouse-input desync/stutter and add input lag on Windows 11 - the opposite of the intended effect. De-recommended; gated to Win10 desktops and kept reversible for tuners who want to test it.
tweaks.rationale: Older guides forced the constant tick for frame pacing, but Microsoft lists disabledynamictick as debugging-only and current testing (Blur Busters forums) ties it to mouse desync and added latency on Win11. Removed from the Frame Pacing and Asta presets in v0.2.6 and gated to Win10 (osMaxBuild 19045) so it is no longer recommended on Win11. Fully reversible to default.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental debug-only BCD flag. It can create mouse desync or stutter and is not a general frame-pacing fix. Win10-only targeting does not make it risk-free.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May change idle timer behavior on a narrow legacy setup; current Windows 11 evidence points toward no benefit or worse input.

tweaks.title: BCD: TSC Sync Policy = Enhanced
tweaks.description: Forces Windows to use the enhanced TSC synchronization policy across CPU cores. Reduces TSC drift on multi-CCD / multi-die parts (Ryzen, Threadripper).
tweaks.rationale: From diggy-tweaks/cpu. Default policy can let TSC drift between dies on AMD chiplets; Enhanced syncs aggressively. Lower 0.1% lows on Ryzen specifically.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental BCD flag. Microsoft documents this option as debugging-only; test boot, clock stability, and tournament anti-cheat compatibility before keeping it.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Possible multi-die timer behavior change; no universal FPS or input-latency win is guaranteed.

tweaks.title: Disable Power Throttling
tweaks.description: Tells Windows to never throttle background processes for power. Removes the EcoQoS scheduler bias on idle apps that can stall game-process wake-ups.
tweaks.rationale: Cross-validated across fr33thy + lecctron + xilly. Power Throttling can briefly demote game threads when alt-tabbing or when GPU presents stall. Off = consistent thread priority.

tweaks.title: Allow Process-Level Timer Resolution Requests
tweaks.description: Restores Windows 10 1909+ behavior where any process can drop the system timer to 0.5ms via NtSetTimerResolution. Required for TimerResolution.exe + QuickCPU + per-game timer-res hacks to actually take effect.
tweaks.rationale: Win10/11 changed timer resolution to be per-process for power reasons. This reg flag opts back into the legacy global-low-timer-res mode. From reknotic + xilly transcripts; pre-condition for any user-mode timer-res tool.

tweaks.title: Disable Spectre/Meltdown Mitigations (DANGER)
tweaks.description: Turns off only the selected Windows Spectre v2 + Meltdown mitigations. This is not a command to disable every Windows exploit mitigation, and it is never part of automatic Tune Now.
tweaks.rationale: Cross-validated across fr33thy + lecctron + xilly. **Audited 2026-05-07**: `FeatureSettingsOverride=3 + Mask=3` is the original 2018 KB4072698 guidance — covers Spectre v2 + Meltdown ONLY. Does NOT cover MDS / Downfall / L1TF / Retbleed (those need different bit values like Override=72 or 8264 per current MS guidance). Pure performance tradeoff. Apply ONLY on dedicated gaming PCs with no untrusted browsers / mail / VMs. NEVER on shared/work machines. Almost no win on AMD (Meltdown didn't affect AMD); we hard-target Intel.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Extreme security tradeoff. This re-exposes CPU side-channel mitigations and may affect anti-cheat, browsers, work apps, VMs, and future Windows support. Use only on a dedicated offline-first gaming rig with a restore point.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce CPU overhead on some Intel rigs; it does not repair a degraded CPU and may produce no measurable game gain.

tweaks.title: Disable Fault-Tolerant Heap recovery (troubleshooting only)
tweaks.description: Stops Windows Diagnostic Policy Service from applying its Fault-Tolerant Heap recovery path for handled heap-corruption scenarios. It does not make games faster.
tweaks.rationale: Fault-Tolerant Heap exists to keep unstable legacy applications running and to aid diagnosis. Disabling it can remove a compatibility safety net; only use it to reproduce a specific application problem, then revert.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Compatibility and stability tradeoff. Do not use as a general gaming optimization; keep it off the automatic presets.
tweaks.expectedImpact: No expected FPS or input-latency gain. May change how a faulty application fails.

tweaks.title: Disable USB Selective-Suspend Power Management
tweaks.description: Stops Windows from entering selective-suspend on USB hub devices. On an affected setup this may avoid a resume stall, but it is not a fixed input-latency reduction.
tweaks.rationale: Cross-validated across fr33thy + xilly. Selective-suspend behavior varies by controller, hub, device, and power plan; compare input traces and power/resume behavior on the actual rig.

tweaks.title: Disable HID Power Management
tweaks.description: Companion to the USB power-mgmt tweak — covers HID-class devices (mouse, keyboard, controllers) at the driver layer.
tweaks.rationale: Cross-validated across fr33thy + lecctron. Apply alongside the USB selective-suspend tweak; without this, HID-class devices can still selective-suspend independently.

tweaks.title: Enable Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)
tweaks.description: Turns on HAGS at the driver layer so the GPU can manage more of its own VRAM scheduling. It can change frame-time behavior on supported drivers, but the result is workload- and driver-dependent; compare it with a repeatable game run.
tweaks.rationale: Cross-validated across fr33thy + lestripez transcripts. HAGS is on by default on Win11 22H2+ but off on many Win10 / older Win11 builds. Forces it on. Pairs well with NVIDIA Reflex and DirectStorage.

tweaks.title: Disable Auto-Capture / Clip Recording
tweaks.description: Disables the auto-clip recorder that runs alongside Game DVR. Distinct from the main Game DVR toggle — kills the always-on circular-buffer capture process.
tweaks.rationale: From reknotic. Even with Game DVR off, AppCaptureEnabled can still spin a buffer process that holds GPU resources. Off = full GameDVR shutdown.

tweaks.title: Disable Memory Compression (MMAgent)
tweaks.description: Turns off Windows' compressed-memory background process. It may reduce compression work when a system has ample RAM, but can increase paging or memory pressure elsewhere; keep it as an Asta experiment and measure.
tweaks.rationale: MMAgent's memory-compression saves RAM at the cost of constant CPU work. On 16GB+ rigs, the trade goes the wrong way for gaming. From fr33thy + xilly transcripts. Reversible.

actions.apply: Disable-MMAgent -mc
actions.revert: Enable-MMAgent -mc

tweaks.title: Add 'DT Tournament' Power Plan
tweaks.description: Idempotently activates a named clone of the hidden Ultimate Performance scheme. If 'DT Tournament' already exists, the action reuses it instead of creating duplicates. Same Windows power primitives as Ultimate Performance; BIOS thermal limits and per-core boost protections remain active. Revert removes only the named clone.
tweaks.rationale: Win10/11 ships Ultimate Performance hidden unless on Enterprise/Workstation SKUs. We duplicate, then rename the clone so users can see at a glance which plan came from us. NOTE: 'doesn't fry the PC' is misleading — neither this plan nor any power plan can override BIOS thermal/power limits. The motherboard's PL1/PL2/IccMax + the CPU's thermal trip-point are still active. We just stop Windows from voluntarily under-clocking.

tweaks.title: Disable Page Combining (MMAgent)
tweaks.description: Stops Windows from scanning RAM for identical pages and merging them. Pairs with the Disable-MMAgent -mc tweak — together they fully disable Win10/11's RAM-deduplication background work.
tweaks.rationale: Page combining runs every few minutes and walks the entire memory map. On 16GB+ rigs the CPU cost outweighs the RAM savings. Cross-validated by fr33thy + xilly.

actions.apply: Disable-MMAgent -PageCombining
actions.revert: Enable-MMAgent -PageCombining

tweaks.title: Disable SysMain (Superfetch)
tweaks.description: Stops the SysMain service. SysMain is the modern name for Superfetch and its value depends on the drive, workload, and Windows build.
tweaks.rationale: Microsoft documents cases where SysMain can spike CPU, but there is no universal NVMe or FPS win from disabling it. Treat this as an advanced diagnostic switch: measure disk activity, frametimes, and app launch behavior before keeping it.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Advanced compatibility experiment. Re-enable SysMain if application launches, caching, or background behavior worsens.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce a specific SysMain CPU spike; no general gaming-performance guarantee.

tweaks.title: Disable Windows Search Indexer
tweaks.description: Stops the WSearch indexing service. This removes automatic indexing but also makes Windows search results slower or incomplete until indexing is restored.
tweaks.rationale: Microsoft recommends reducing indexed locations and excluding high-churn folders before disabling indexing globally. Use this only when measured indexing activity is a real problem and you have another search workflow.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Advanced background-activity experiment. Prefer selective indexing/exclusions for a normal Windows installation.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May remove indexing disk/CPU activity; no guaranteed FPS or input-latency gain.

tweaks.title: BCD: Silent Boot (Skip Boot Logo)
tweaks.description: Tells the Windows boot loader to skip the rotating-dots boot animation. Minor boot-time win + cleaner POST → game-ready handoff.
tweaks.rationale: Saves ~0.5s of boot time and removes the post-bootloader animation that some Quick Resume rigs flicker through. Safe and fully reversible.

tweaks.title: Disable Microsoft Edge Background Mode
tweaks.description: Stops Edge from running background extension hosts and update probes when no Edge windows are open. Frees ~50-200 MB and several background threads on stock Win11.
tweaks.rationale: Edge keeps a hidden 'background mode' process alive even after you close all windows — used for sync, push notifications, and update polling. Off = clean shutdown when you close the last window.

tweaks.title: Disable Microsoft Store app background activity
tweaks.description: Applies the Windows policy that denies background execution for Store apps. Traditional desktop applications are not controlled by this policy.
tweaks.rationale: Useful for a deliberately quiet gaming profile, but it can affect notifications, sync, Search/Cortana, and other Store-based components. It is a background-activity choice, not a guaranteed FPS improvement.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: May suppress notifications, synchronization, and background features. Keep this explicit and revert if an app stops updating or notifying.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Fewer Store-app background tasks; no guaranteed in-game latency gain.

tweaks.title: Disable automatic Windows Update (advanced)
tweaks.description: Writes the Windows Update policy that disables automatic update scanning. It is not a permanent guarantee: Windows, device management, and policy refreshes can change it, and it also blocks important security fixes.
tweaks.rationale: There is no supported forever-pause mode. Use only when you accept manual patching and have a maintenance plan. Prefer pausing/deferring updates around competition rather than disabling security servicing indefinitely.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: High maintenance and security cost. You must manually check, install, and restart for security updates; managed PCs may ignore or overwrite this policy.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Fewer update interruptions; no FPS or input-latency gain.

tweaks.title: Disable Microsoft Store (advanced)
tweaks.description: Blocks the Microsoft Store application through the Windows policy used by Pro/Enterprise management. Store app updates and Store UI access stop until reverted.
tweaks.rationale: This can keep an intentionally minimal machine from opening Store surfaces, but it has no expected gaming-performance benefit and may interfere with Store-delivered apps or updates. winget and other installers may still work.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Blocks Store access and Store updates. Do not use if you rely on Xbox, Store, or Store-delivered app updates.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Less Store UI/background activity; no expected FPS or input-latency gain.

tweaks.title: Disable Discord Auto-Start
tweaks.description: Removes Discord from the login Run key so it doesn't auto-launch + auto-update on boot. Discord still works on-demand.
tweaks.rationale: Discord's startup runs the auto-updater (constant network/disk on slow rigs) plus loads the full Electron shell into memory before you even open a chat. Off = launch when you actually need it.

tweaks.title: Disable Steam Auto-Start
tweaks.description: Removes Steam from the login Run key. Steam still launches when you click a game shortcut or run steam.exe directly — just doesn't auto-boot.
tweaks.rationale: Steam's auto-start spins up the full client + every shader pre-cache + family-view sync immediately on login. Multi-GB of disk read + steady network for 60s after boot. Off = no idle Steam tax.

tweaks.title: Disable Bing Web Search in Start Menu
tweaks.description: Stops the Win10/11 Start menu from sending your typed text to Bing. Search becomes local-only — apps + files + settings, no web roundtrip.
tweaks.rationale: Every keystroke in Start is uploaded to Bing for 'web suggestions'. Off = privacy + zero network roundtrips on every keystroke. Distinct from Cortana service disable — that kills the service, this kills the search-uploads-to-bing pipeline.

tweaks.title: Disable OneDrive Auto-Start
tweaks.description: Removes OneDrive from the Run key so it doesn't auto-launch on login. OneDrive still works on-demand if you launch it manually.
tweaks.rationale: OneDrive's startup probe + initial folder sync wakes the disk + network on every boot. Even with no files synced, the daemon polls Microsoft endpoints every few minutes.

tweaks.title: Disable Win11 Transparency Effects
tweaks.description: Turns off the acrylic/blur compositor effects in the Win11 taskbar, Start menu, and notification center. Removes the per-frame GPU blur passes.
tweaks.rationale: Acrylic blur is composited while Explorer surfaces are visible and may matter on shared-GPU systems. The cost is usually small and workload-dependent; no fixed GPU percentage is promised.

tweaks.title: Disable Sticky / Filter / Toggle Keys Shortcuts
tweaks.description: Removes the 'Press Shift 5x' StickyKeys popup, the FilterKeys hold-key shortcut, and the ToggleKeys beeps. The accessibility prompts that pop up mid-game and steal focus.
tweaks.rationale: Every gamer's nightmare — Shift-spam in a melee burst triggers the StickyKeys dialog, which steals window focus and breaks input until you alt-tab. Off = never see it again. Accessibility features themselves stay functional via Settings → Ease of Access if you ever turn them on intentionally.

tweaks.title: Disable Modern Standby (Force S3 Sleep)
tweaks.description: Forces the platform to use the traditional S3 sleep state instead of Modern Standby (S0ix). Sleep actually sleeps — no background wake-from-sleep cycles draining battery / waking GPU.
tweaks.rationale: Modern Standby keeps a 'connected' state running while the screen is off, allowing background sync but causing real wake-cycle drain on desktops that don't need it. S3 is the classic 'really off' sleep. Off = predictable sleep behavior, fans actually stop.

tweaks.title: Disable Win11 Recall (AI Snapshots)
tweaks.description: Stops the Win11 24H2+ Recall feature from taking continuous screenshots + indexing them with the on-device AI model. The well-known privacy / security disaster that Microsoft shipped quietly.
tweaks.rationale: Recall takes screenshots every few seconds and stores them in a local DB. While encrypted, the attack surface (and battery + GPU + disk drain) is real. Off = no screenshot capture, no AI indexing, no Copilot+PC overhead. Required reading before applying: Microsoft's own Recall security disclosures.

tweaks.title: Disable Cloud-Content Promos + 3rd-Party Suggestions
tweaks.description: Disables CloudContent consumer features (movie/app promos, OS feature pushes) and third-party Start-menu suggestions. Reduces network calls + promo surfaces.
tweaks.rationale: This entry removes consumer promos and third-party suggestions; it does not change lock-screen image rotation. Use the separate lock-screen Spotlight entry when that is the actual goal. The performance effect is cosmetic.

tweaks.title: Disable Windows Spotlight on the lock screen
tweaks.description: Stops rotating Windows Spotlight images and suggestions on the lock screen. This is separate from the Start-menu consumer-content policy above.
tweaks.rationale: A cosmetic/privacy choice with no meaningful gaming-performance mechanism. Use it if you want a static lock screen and fewer suggestion surfaces, not as an FPS tweak.

tweaks.title: Hide Taskbar Search Box
tweaks.description: Collapses the always-on taskbar search box into a small icon. Reclaims taskbar real estate + removes the always-rendered search field from the compositor's hot path.
tweaks.rationale: The taskbar search box renders on every Explorer redraw + holds keyboard focus when accidentally clicked mid-game. Hidden mode keeps Win+S shortcut working but reclaims the pixels. Win10/11 universal.

tweaks.title: Disable Wake Timers
tweaks.description: Stops scheduled tasks and Windows Update from waking the PC out of sleep. It does not disable sleep itself.
tweaks.rationale: Use this when unexpected wake-ups are the problem. Sleep Study is a diagnostic report, not a performance tweak; run powercfg /sleepstudy to identify wake and residency causes before changing sleep policy.

tweaks.title: Disable News and Interests Taskbar Feed
tweaks.description: Stops the Win10 22H2+ taskbar weather/news feed from polling Microsoft endpoints + rendering its widget. Reclaims taskbar real estate + a steady network heartbeat.
tweaks.rationale: News and Interests fetches every few minutes and renders a widget on every Explorer paint. Off on most pro rigs. Distinct from Win11 Widgets — this is the Win10 taskbar version.

tweaks.title: Disable Storage Sense Auto-Cleanup
tweaks.description: Stops Storage Sense from auto-emptying Recycle Bin, Downloads, and old OneDrive cloud-only files on a schedule. Lets you control your own cleanup.
tweaks.rationale: Storage Sense runs in the background, scans every drive, and auto-deletes 'unused' files. On rigs with predictable workflow it deletes things you actually wanted. Off = you decide when to clean.

tweaks.title: Disable Win11 Snap Layouts Hover Popup
tweaks.description: Stops the Snap Layouts grid from popping up when you hover over a window's maximize button. Win+Z still works if you want it.
tweaks.rationale: The hover-trigger fires on every accidental near-pass of the maximize button — pure friction during gameplay window-switching. Off = no popup, no flash, hotkey still available.

tweaks.title: Disable Clipboard Cloud Sync
tweaks.description: Stops the Win10/11 cloud clipboard from uploading copied text/images to your Microsoft account for cross-device sync. Local clipboard history (Win+V) still works.
tweaks.rationale: Cloud clipboard uploads literally everything you copy to Microsoft — including passwords, secrets, paste-buffer contents during dev work. Off = local-only clipboard, no upload. Win+V history still functional.

tweaks.title: Disable Hibernation
tweaks.description: Turns off hibernation and removes hiberfil.sys. This also removes Fast Startup, so use it only when you specifically want the disk space or a true full shutdown.
tweaks.rationale: There is no general gaming-performance win. Keep hibernation on when you use hibernate or Fast Startup; on a desktop, disabling it is an optional clean-shutdown/storage choice.

actions.apply: powercfg /h off
actions.revert: powercfg /h on

tweaks.title: Disable Automatic Windows Driver Updates
tweaks.description: Stops Windows Update from automatically installing device drivers through its driver-update policy. It does not disable Windows quality or security updates.
tweaks.rationale: Useful when you intentionally stage GPU, audio, or chipset drivers yourself. Keep a manual driver-maintenance plan; this policy can leave devices on an old driver.

tweaks.title: Disable Windows SmartScreen
tweaks.description: Turns off the SmartScreen reputation-based executable filter. Lets unsigned utilities and custom binaries run without the 'Windows protected your PC' warning + click-through gate.
tweaks.rationale: SmartScreen makes a network call to Microsoft on EVERY new-binary launch. Power users running custom tools, crypto wallets, or self-built utilities pay a 0.5-2s startup tax for the privilege of an upload. Off = no network roundtrip on launch.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Security experiment. SmartScreen blocks or warns on suspicious downloads; disabling it increases exposure to malicious or tampered binaries. Keep it on unless you have a specific test case.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May remove a launch warning or reputation check, not improve Fortnite frame time or input latency.

tweaks.title: Disable Internet-Zone Download Warning
tweaks.description: Stops File Explorer from blocking downloaded files until you right-click → Unblock. Saves a manual click on every legit download from a non-MOTW source.
tweaks.rationale: The 'this file came from the Internet' MOTW gate is a security feature for office users; for power users running custom tools and patches it's pure friction. Off = no per-file unblock dance. Audited 2026-05-07: prior catalog had value=1 inverted, which preserved zone info; corrected to 2 (strip on save).

tweaks.title: Disable Multi-Plane Overlay (MPO)
tweaks.description: Conditional fix, not an FPS lever. Forces DWM to composite normally instead of using GPU plane overlays. Apply ONLY if you see multi-monitor stuttering or black-screen/flicker (a known MPO bug on some VRR setups). On a healthy single-monitor rig, disabling MPO can cost the low-latency Independent Flip path, so leave it on unless you have the problem.
tweaks.rationale: MPO is a presentation optimization; on most rigs it is harmless or helpful (it enables Independent Flip). It only backfires on certain dual-monitor + variable-refresh configs where the plane scheduler conflicts with G-Sync/FreeSync, producing flicker/stutter. This tweak is the fix for that specific bug, not a general performance gain. On Windows 11 24H2 the OverlayTestMode=5 write alone is unreliable, so we also set OverlayMinFPS=0. Reversible.

tweaks.title: Disable Win11 Optimizations for Windowed Games
tweaks.description: Turns off Win11's per-game windowed-mode optimizations (the Auto-HDR + Variable-Refresh / DirectFlip hint layer) via the DirectX user settings. CONDITIONAL fix: only worth applying if a specific title stutters when this layer activates mid-frame. On a healthy single-monitor rig it can COST input latency on 24H2 (26100+), where this layer IS the low-latency DirectFlip path that replaced fullscreen-exclusive - leave it ON unless you have a measured stutter.
tweaks.rationale: Win11 22H2 added a windowed-game optimization shim that intercepts present calls. Audited 2026-06-25: prior catalog wrote the unrecognized token `GlobalOptimizationsFlags=0` which Windows ignores - the tweak was inert and the optimization stayed ON. Corrected to the real tokens `SwapEffectUpgradeEnable=0;VRROptimizeEnable=0;` (MS Support 'Optimizations for windowed games in Windows 11'; Winhance #363). Reframed as a conditional stutter-fix, not a blanket latency win - on 24H2 this layer is the DirectFlip low-latency path.

tweaks.title: BCD: Disable Hyper-V Hypervisor at Boot
tweaks.description: Stops the Hyper-V hypervisor from loading at boot. Removes VBS/HVCI overhead even with Memory Integrity left enabled in Windows Security.
tweaks.rationale: From diggy-tweaks/cpu. A loaded hypervisor can affect virtualization-sensitive workloads, but Windows build, features, firmware, and workload determine the result; do not assume a fixed CPU or FPS gain.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental boot change. It disables the Windows hypervisor and can break VBS-dependent security, virtualization, WSL, sandboxing, or competitive anti-cheat requirements until reverted and rebooted.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce virtualization overhead on CPU-bound workloads; measure on your rig instead of assuming a fixed FPS gain.

tweaks.title: NIC: Interrupt Moderation = Disabled
tweaks.description: Disables NIC-level interrupt coalescing on every physical adapter that exposes the property. This may reduce local packet batching on some workloads, at the cost of more interrupts and CPU; it is not a guarantee of the lowest end-to-end latency.
tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/network. Of the NIC offload knobs this is the one with a plausible mechanism: default coalescing batches up to ~256 µs of packets to reduce CPU load, disabled = immediate interrupt delivery. Honest caveat (2026): competitive netcode is small UDP and end-to-end ping/jitter is ISP/route-dominated, so the real-world win is marginal and CPU-spent-in-DPC rises - not the headline win older guides claim. Worth it on a CPU with headroom; skip if CPU-bound. Pair with core-parking-disable so a parked core doesn't have to wake first.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental NIC interrupt setting. It can raise DPC/CPU load and the old inverse guessed Enabled/Adaptive. The app now records each adapter's prior display value; revert and re-test if CPU frametimes or network stability worsen.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce local interrupt batching on a CPU with headroom; it cannot lower ISP ping and may make a CPU-bound rig worse.

tweaks.title: NIC: Flow Control = Disabled
tweaks.description: Turns off Ethernet pause-frame Flow Control on every up-physical NIC. Switches stop being able to ask the NIC to pause; queue management becomes the host's job.
tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/network. Flow Control's pause frames add jitter on consumer switches that misbehave under load. Pros disable to keep the NIC always-sending. Safe on dedicated gaming switches; can cause drop bursts on enterprise QoS gear — keep on if your switch is managing your VoIP.

tweaks.title: NIC: Receive Side Scaling = Enabled
tweaks.description: Force-enables Receive Side Scaling on every up-physical adapter. Spreads incoming-packet processing across CPU cores instead of pinning to core 0.
tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/network. Default-on most modern NICs but vendor drivers sometimes flip off after updates. Idempotent re-enable. Without RSS the network stack is a single-core bottleneck under high pps — multiplayer match servers can saturate it.

tweaks.title: Disable CPU Core Parking (100% min cores)
tweaks.description: Sets the minimum-active-cores power-plan setting to 100% on both AC and DC. Windows scheduler keeps every core spun up — no parking, no wake-from-park latency penalty when a game thread suddenly needs another core.
tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/cpu (Bitsum ParkControl recommendation). The native equivalent of ParkControl's 'Disable parking' without a third-party tool. Wake-from-park = 50-200 µs latency spike when a parked core needs to handle an interrupt or a new thread; disabling = no spike at the cost of slightly higher idle power.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental power-plan change. It keeps cores active and can raise idle power, heat, and laptop battery drain; Windows scheduling may already be better for your rig.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce wake-up behavior in a narrow latency-sensitive case, but can do nothing or hurt thermals.

tweaks.rationale: Use only when device wake/resume behavior is a measured problem. Windows still manages CPU idle states; forcing every device to stay fully active can raise idle power and heat without improving a game.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Advanced power-plan experiment. It can increase idle power, heat, and laptop battery drain; keep the normal Balanced/Ultimate defaults unless testing shows a benefit.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce device power-state transitions; no general FPS, ping, or input-latency guarantee.

tweaks.title: Disable PCIe Link State Power Management (ASPM Off)
tweaks.description: Sets PCI Express ASPM (Active State Power Management) to Off on the current power plan. PCIe lanes stay at full power instead of dropping to L0s/L1 between transfers.
tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/gpu. ASPM transitions add 5-20 µs latency on every PCIe burst. GPU + NVMe + NIC all sit on PCIe — the fix is global. Tradeoff: a few watts of idle power. Worth it on a desktop, defer on laptops.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental power-plan change. It keeps PCIe links awake and raises idle power; revert and check temperatures if the result is not measured as positive.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May avoid link power-state transitions on a desktop; it cannot lower ISP ping and may be irrelevant on a healthy system.

tweaks.rationale: Source: diggy-tweaks/device-tweaks. Pairs with NVIDIA HID-power-disable. Polling-rate-1000Hz wireless mice can lose packets when the USB-3 host controller transitions out of U1/U2; off = constant link state, predictable polling. Combine with `process.usb-power-mgmt.disable` for full coverage.

tweaks.title: Mouse Class: ThreadPriority = Realtime (31)
tweaks.description: Boosts the mouclass kernel worker thread that drains incoming mouse events to realtime priority. Reduces ISR-to-user-thread propagation jitter.
tweaks.rationale: Source: denis-g/windows10-latency-optimization + djdallmann GamingPCSetup. Not Microsoft-documented at the API level — the value is read by the class driver at boot and used to set its worker-thread priority. Safe: the worker just drains a queue, no userland bypass. Pair with `process.usb-power-mgmt.disable` and `power.usb3.link-power.disable` for full input chain coverage.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental kernel worker priority. Reboot is required; a realtime class thread can starve other work if a driver misbehaves.
tweaks.expectedImpact: Possible input-queue jitter reduction, but measure it and revert if frametimes or audio become worse.

tweaks.title: Keyboard Class: ThreadPriority = Realtime (31)
tweaks.description: Same as the mouse-class realtime boost, applied to kbdclass — keyboard worker thread runs at realtime priority for lower input jitter.
tweaks.rationale: Mirror of `hid.mouse.priority-realtime`. Keyboard scheduling behavior is driver- and workload-dependent; raising service priority can affect system responsiveness, so validate it with input traces and a recovery path rather than assuming a fixed quantum or zero cost.

tweaks.title: Disable HVCI / Memory Integrity (VBS off)
tweaks.description: Disables Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity at the registry-policy level. Keep Core isolation and Memory integrity enabled by default; use this only when a specific, incompatible driver or controlled benchmark requires it.
tweaks.rationale: Core isolation protects kernel and driver paths. Microsoft warns that turning Memory integrity off can allow a blocked driver to load but removes that protection; any performance difference is workload-dependent, not a guaranteed FPS gain. Change it only for an explicit lab test, then restore it and reboot.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Experimental security change. It reduces Windows virtualization-based protection and may stop Valorant, FACEIT, BattlEye, or other security-sensitive software from qualifying.
tweaks.expectedImpact: May reduce CPU overhead in CPU-bound workloads; the security and eligibility tradeoff is real.

tweaks.title: Fortnite: launch with High CPU priority (IFEO)
tweaks.description: Image File Execution Options entry that launches FortniteClient-Win64-Shipping.exe with CPU Priority Class = High (3). Persistent across launches — set once, applies forever.
tweaks.rationale: Source: Bitsum + Microsoft IFEO docs. CpuPriorityClass=3 (High) is the safe ceiling — Realtime (4) starves keyboard/mouse input threads and can hard-freeze the rig. High biases the scheduler toward the game without input starvation. Note: the IFEO `Affinity` value people quote is FOLKLORE — only `CpuPriorityClass` actually works.

tweaks.title: NIC: Disable Receive Segment Coalescing (RSC) — fiber
tweaks.description: Disables Receive Segment Coalescing on every up-physical NIC. RSC merges incoming TCP segments into larger ones at the NIC level to reduce CPU interrupt load — but on a high-end fiber connection, modern CPUs can handle the per-segment work and benefit from lower-latency packet delivery vs the coalescing batch delay.
tweaks.rationale: Source: Microsoft Learn `Set-NetAdapterRsc` cmdlet docs + competitive-FPS community testing. RSC was designed for 1Gbps NICs feeding slow CPUs — modern 2.5/10Gbps + Ryzen/Raptor Lake doesn't need the help. Disabling = packets delivered as the NIC receives them, lower latency at slightly higher CPU. Pairs with `net.nic.interrupt-moderation.disable`. Logs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\optmaxxing\nic-tweak.log`.

tweaks.title: NIC: Disable Large Send Offload (LSO)
tweaks.description: Disables Large Send Offload on every up-physical NIC. LSO lets the NIC fragment large outbound TCP segments — disabling it makes the CPU do that work, eliminating one source of NIC-side queuing delay.
tweaks.rationale: LSO is a throughput optimization (helps file transfers + bulk uploads); for game traffic which is usually small UDP packets it does nothing useful, and on some Killer/Realtek consumer NICs the LSO logic introduces measurable latency variance. Tradeoff: slower sustained large uploads. Apply on dedicated gaming rigs; skip on a workstation that's also pulling video uploads.

tweaks.title: Fortnite: generate NVIDIA Profile Inspector profile (.nip)
tweaks.description: Writes a conservative, verified per-game NVIDIA driver profile for the Fortnite profile (FortniteClient-Win64-Shipping.exe + FortniteLauncher.exe) to %LOCALAPPDATA%\optmaxxing\nvpi\Fortnite.nip and opens the folder. Profile sets: Power Management = Prefer Maximum Performance (pins clocks, improves frametime consistency), Texture Filtering Quality = High Performance, Vertical Sync = Force Off, Max Pre-Rendered Frames (Low Latency) = use 3D-app default (defer to in-game Reflex). This driver-layer baseline remains applicable to Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4: Override, but major season and driver updates still require a same-scene re-test. After export, open NVIDIA Profile Inspector and import it explicitly; the app does not launch NVPI or write its driver database. Revert deletes the generated file.
tweaks.rationale: Source: Epic 2026 competitive guide + prosettings.net consensus; SettingIDs/values verified against the Orbmu2k/nvidiaProfileInspector source DB + a real .nip export. 'Prefer Maximum Performance' is the high-confidence win -- it stops the GPU downclocking between frames, which is a frametime-consistency (1% low) improvement, not a guaranteed average-FPS gain. We deliberately leave the driver DB untouched and hand you a ready profile instead. Open NVIDIA Profile Inspector yourself, import the file, and Apply changes; do not assume a downloaded file has changed the driver. Leave driver Low Latency Mode at the app default and let in-game Reflex own latency -- driver queue overrides can fight native Reflex. See the NVIDIA Profile Inspector guide for the full walkthrough. Reverse it by importing NVIDIA's defaults in NVPI; deleting the file here just removes our copy.

actions.apply: $d = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\optmaxxing\nvpi"; if (-not (Test-Path $d)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $d -Force | Out-Null }; $p = "$d\Fortnite.nip"; $xml = "<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-16'?><ArrayOfProfile xmlns:xsi='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance' xmlns:xsd='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema'><Profile><ProfileName>Fortnite</ProfileName><Executeables><string>FortniteClient-Win64-Shipping.exe</string><string>FortniteLauncher.exe</string></Executeables><Settings><ProfileSetting><SettingNameInfo>Power management mode</SettingNameInfo><SettingID>274197361</SettingID><SettingValue>1</SettingValue><ValueType>Dword</ValueType></ProfileSetting><ProfileSetting><SettingNameInfo>Texture filtering - Quality</SettingNameInfo><SettingID>13510289</SettingID><SettingValue>20</SettingValue><ValueType>Dword</ValueType></ProfileSetting><ProfileSetting><SettingNameInfo>Vertical Sync</SettingNameInfo><SettingID>11041231</SettingID><SettingValue>138504007</SettingValue><ValueType>Dword</ValueType></ProfileSetting><ProfileSetting><SettingNameInfo>Maximum pre-rendered frames</SettingNameInfo><SettingID>8102046</SettingID><SettingValue>0</SettingValue><ValueType>Dword</ValueType></ProfileSetting></Settings></Profile></ArrayOfProfile>"; [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $xml, [System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode); Start-Process explorer.exe $d
actions.revert: $p = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\optmaxxing\nvpi\Fortnite.nip"; if (Test-Path $p) { Remove-Item $p -Force }

tweaks.title: CS2: competitive autoexec.cfg
tweaks.description: Writes a converged-pro autoexec.cfg to the CS2 cfg folder. Locks raw input on, m_customaccel off, rate 786432, fps_max 0, mat_queue_mode 2 (multithreaded), snd_mixahead 0.025 for tighter audio-cue timing. (v1.9.0: removed the cl_cmdrate/cl_updaterate/cl_interp block — CS2 is sub-tick; those CS:GO cvars are deprecated/non-functional and interp is handled by the menu buffer slider.)
tweaks.rationale: Source: pro CS2 configs (ZywOo/s1mple/NiKo/m0nesy) for the still-valid cvars. The real levers are m_rawinput 1, m_customaccel 0, rate 786432, mat_queue_mode 2 (forces multithreaded render — a few Source 2 rigs fail to multithread without it), and snd_mixahead. fps_max 0 lets the GPU run uncapped (use an NVCP frame cap per the Reflex whitepaper). The old 128-tick / cl_interp 0 / cl_interp_ratio 1 trio was CS:GO cargo-cult — CS2's sub-tick netcode ignores client tickrate cvars, so we no longer write them. Reverts cleanly via the FileWrite snapshot store.

tweaks.title: Apex: competitive videoconfig.txt
tweaks.description: Writes a stripped videoconfig.txt to %USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\Respawn\Apex\local\. Disables gibs, ragdoll collision, particle multipliers, film grain, dynamic vertical sync, cascade shadow maps, dynamic super-sampling. **After applying, manually `attrib +R` the file** so the game can't overwrite — Apex rewrites videoconfig on launch otherwise.
tweaks.rationale: Source: Aceu / sweet / ImperialHal config posts, cross-validated against r/CompetitiveApex pinned threads. These values can change rendering work, but any frame-time effect varies by patch and hardware. Apex may rewrite videoconfig.txt at launch, so this remains an explicit-only preset and must be rechecked in-game.

tweaks.title: Fortnite: competitive Engine.ini
tweaks.description: Writes a competitive-baseline Engine.ini to %LOCALAPPDATA%\FortniteGame\Saved\Config\WindowsClient\. Forces post-processing / shadow / view-distance / effects / foliage scalability to 0, motion blur off, anti-aliasing off, anisotropy off, mesh LOD bias maxed (so distant geometry stays simple). Logs muted. Snapshot-backed revert restores whatever Engine.ini was there before. NOTE (2026): the single biggest Fortnite FPS lever is in-game Performance Mode (DX11), which bypasses Nanite/Lumen — this config can't set it; enable it in Video settings for the largest gain, then these .ini tunes stack on top.
tweaks.rationale: Source: published pro configs and community guides converge on some of these values, but that is not proof of a fixed FPS gain. The settings can change rendering work and may help a CPU- or effects-bound run; compare repeatable 1% lows and visual quality on your own patch. Reverts cleanly via the FileWrite snapshot store. Lives in the user-profile path, no admin needed.

tweaks.title: Fortnite: competitive GameUserSettings.ini
tweaks.description: Explicit-only legacy preset. Pairs with Engine.ini and writes a fixed 240 FPS cap, 1920x1080 resolution, VSync-off, motion-blur-off, HDR-off, and Fullscreen values to GameUserSettings.ini. Those values are not derived from the scanned monitor, resolution, or measured frame pacing, so Tune Now never applies this file automatically. Snapshot-backed revert restores the prior file byte-for-byte.
tweaks.rationale: Fortnite's settings file can be useful for a deliberate, per-rig starting point, but there is no universal best cap, resolution, or window mode. This preset must be checked in-game against the user's display/VRR setup after each Fortnite update; do not mark the file read-only as a default because that blocks legitimate settings changes and can conflict with future updates.
tweaks.experimentalWarning: Fixed values are not a universal Fortnite baseline. Confirm resolution, frame cap, VRR/VSync, and Fullscreen behavior in-game after applying; Tune Now keeps this preset explicit-only.

tweaks.title: Disable RGB control apps at startup (Aura / iCUE / Mystic Light / Synapse / G-Hub / T-Force Blitz / NZXT CAM / OpenRGB / SignalRGB)
tweaks.description: Sweeps every Run/RunOnce autostart entry in HKCU + HKLM (plus WOW6432Node) AND every Scheduled Task whose name matches a known RGB control-app keyword (Aura, Armoury Crate, iCUE, Mystic Light, MSI Center, RGB Fusion, AORUS, Razer Synapse, Logitech G HUB, T-Force, BLITZ, NZXT CAM, EVGA Precision, Cooler Master MasterPlus, OpenRGB, SignalRGB, OMEN Lighting, AlienFX). Each match is stashed to %LOCALAPPDATA%\optmaxxing\backups\rgb-autostart-stash.json before removal — revert restores Run-key values + re-enables tasks. The apps still launch on demand; they just don't auto-spawn at login.
tweaks.rationale: RGB control software is the actual input-delay tax people blame on RGB. The LEDs themselves draw ~negligible USB bus time. The vendor apps polling at 60-1000Hz to push color frames + monitor temps DO cause measurable DPC spikes and 50-200MB+ steady RAM (iCUE and Razer Synapse are repeat offenders — Hardware Unboxed + Gamers Nexus DPC pulls have shown 200µs+ spikes correlated with iCUE running). Companion guide /guides/rgb-shutoff covers persistent LED-off via save-to-flash so you never need to launch the vendor app again after the one-time setup. Two halves of the same fix — this tweak handles the software tax, the guide handles the lighting.

actions.apply: $ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue'; $stashDir="$env:LOCALAPPDATA\optmaxxing\backups"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stashDir -Force | Out-Null; $stashFile="$stashDir\rgb-autostart-stash.json"; $kw=@('Aura','Armoury','ArmouryCrate','ROG Live','LightingService','iCUE','Corsair','Mystic','MSI Center','RGB Fusion','GIGABYTE Control','AORUS','Razer','RzPlatform','Logitech G HUB','LGHUB','T-Force','TForce','BLITZ','NZXT CAM','NZXT','EVGA Precision','MasterPlus','Cooler Master','OpenRGB','SignalRGB','OMEN Lighting','OmenLighting','AlienFX','Alienware Command'); $runKeys=@('HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run','HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce','HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run','HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce','HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'); $stash=@{runKeyEntries=@();scheduledTasks=@()}; foreach ($p in $runKeys) { if (-not (Test-Path $p)) { continue }; $props=Get-ItemProperty -Path $p; foreach ($n in $props.PSObject.Properties.Name) { if ($n -like 'PS*') { continue }; $hay="$n $($props.$n)"; $hit=$false; foreach ($k in $kw) { if ($hay -like "*$k*") { $hit=$true; break } }; if ($hit) { $stash.runKeyEntries+=@{key=$p;name=$n;data=[string]$props.$n}; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Force } } }; try { $tasks=Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction Stop; foreach ($t in $tasks) { if ([string]$t.State -eq 'Disabled') { continue }; $hay="$($t.TaskName) $($t.TaskPath)"; $hit=$false; foreach ($k in $kw) { if ($hay -like "*$k*") { $hit=$true; break } }; if ($hit) { $stash.scheduledTasks+=@{path=$t.TaskPath;name=$t.TaskName}; Disable-ScheduledTask -TaskPath $t.TaskPath -TaskName $t.TaskName | Out-Null } } } catch {}; ($stash | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6) | Set-Content -Path $stashFile -Encoding UTF8; Write-Output ("OK removed="+$stash.runKeyEntries.Count+" disabledTasks="+$stash.scheduledTasks.Count)
actions.revert: $ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue'; $stashFile="$env:LOCALAPPDATA\optmaxxing\backups\rgb-autostart-stash.json"; if (-not (Test-Path $stashFile)) { Write-Output 'NOSTASH'; return }; $stash=Get-Content $stashFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json; foreach ($e in $stash.runKeyEntries) { if (-not (Test-Path $e.key)) { New-Item -Path $e.key -Force | Out-Null }; New-ItemProperty -Path $e.key -Name $e.name -Value $e.data -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null }; foreach ($t in $stash.scheduledTasks) { try { Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskPath $t.path -TaskName $t.name | Out-Null } catch {} }; Remove-Item $stashFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Output 'OK'

tweaks.title: USB pinnacle — kill interrupt coalescing + selective suspend + boost HID/mouse/keyboard IRQ priority
tweaks.description: Seven registry writes that together pull USB devices (mouse, keyboard, HID controllers) onto the lowest-latency path Windows exposes. Disables USB Selective Suspend at three driver layers (root USB / USB 2.0 hub / USB 3.0 hub), promotes the HID service to boot-start so it's loaded before the desktop session, and raises IRQ priority on mouclass / kbdclass / HidUsb so their interrupts get scheduled ahead of background drivers. Single UAC. Every value snapshot-backed for byte-perfect revert.
tweaks.rationale: Documented input-lag stack from PC-Tuning + Calypto + Xiseous guides. Disabling Selective Suspend and changing HID service/priority settings are community mechanisms, not a guaranteed latency result. They are not Microsoft-documented esports requirements; measure input traces, DPC behavior, device stability, and current game eligibility before keeping them.

tweaks.title: Disable Fast Startup (keep hibernation)
tweaks.description: Turns off Windows Fast Startup (hybrid boot) so every shutdown is a true cold boot that reloads a clean kernel + drivers. Sleep and hibernation stay available - this is the lighter-touch alternative to disabling hibernation entirely.
tweaks.rationale: Fast Startup restores a hibernated kernel image on 'shutdown', carrying stale driver/network state between sessions - a known source of intermittent stutter, post-update glitches, and dual-boot clock drift. Disabling via HiberbootEnabled=0 leaves hibernation intact (unlike powercfg /hibernate off) and costs only a couple seconds of boot on an SSD. Reversible: default is 1.
